subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After the atomic authorization defect is repaired, should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every legacy ownerless row, or must a migration or recovery path precede enforcement?
rationale: Exact ownership enforcement closes the security gap but deliberately removes an existing capability for persisted ownerless rows, and repository evidence cannot determine the intended upgrade contract.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery
options.body: Reject ownerless rows while providing a documented operator or doctor recovery path and explicit upgrade proof.

options.title: Migrate eligible rows
options.body: Define a safe ownership migration before enabling exact enforcement for legacy persisted sessions.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows while providing a documented operator or doctor recovery path and explicit upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice intersects the active SQLite session-storage and transaction boundary introduced by this owner’s recent refactor.
